title: Citi upgrades US equities to overweight on defensive tilt, sees 12% upside in S&P 500
text:
15 Trending Topics Sensex Live Kalyan Jewellers Share Price Hindalco Share Price Oil Prices IIFL Finance Share Price Citi upgrades US equities to overweight on defensive tilt, sees 12% upside in S&P 500 Citigroup strategists have upgraded US equities to overweight from neutral on a “quality/defensive tilt” in their global allocation. They also downgraded emerging markets stocks to neutral from overweight, citing vulnerability to energy shocks. Bloomberg April 14, 2026 / 11:04 IST US Stocks Citigroup upgrades US stocks to overweight, citing defensive tilt Emerging markets downgraded due to energy shocks, strong dollar S&P 500 seen reaching 7,700 by year-end, a 12 percent gain Did our AI summary help? Market Mastery Webinar by Vishal Malkan Find the weak links in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan Register for FREE Webinar Register for FREE Citigroup Inc. strategists have joined Wall Street peers in turning more constructive on US stocks, saying elevated war uncertainty supports a preference for higher-quality and defensive companies. Strategists including Beata Manthey upgraded US equities to overweight from neutral on a “quality/defensive tilt” in their global allocation. They also downgraded emerging markets stocks to neutral from overweight, citing vulnerability to energy shocks and a stronger dollar in their report to investors. Citigroup’s move follows similar positive calls at BlackRock Inc. and Morgan Stanley on the US market for its relative resilience. The S&P 500 Index on Monday erased its war-related losses, helped by a temporary US-Iran ceasefire and optimism at the start of the earnings season. The Citi strategists called their US upgrade “tactical” given the limited visibility. They expect the S&P 500 to reach 7,700 by year-end, implying a 12% gain from Monday’s close. Among key sectoral changes they upgraded global materials to overweight and downgraded communication services to underweight. They also highlighted that the technology sector’s growing heft over global earnings growth complicates the equity outlook along with the war. While an eventual peace deal between the US and Iran should lift investor sentiment, “a return to ‘goldilocks’ macro and pro-cyclical trading dynamics may prove difficult,” the strategists wrote.
